The Last Run of the Pony Express An original passage written for LearnAce 1 In October 1861, sixteen-year-old Billy galloped across the Nevada desert with a leather pouch of letters strapped to his saddle. Riders like him changed horses every fifteen kilometres so the mail could cross the country in just ten days. 2 At the station, the keeper handed him a cup of water and some news. "Telegraph lines reached California today," he said. "Messages can cross the country in minutes now." 3 Billy looked at the thin wire stretched along the poles. He patted his tired horse. examples.question: Ice Skates on the Rideau An original passage written for LearnAce 1 In the winter of 1910, Marie laced up her father's old skates on the frozen Rideau Canal in Ottawa. Her skates were too big, so she stuffed her mother's knitted socks into the toes. 2 Back then, there were no snow-clearing machines on the canal. Families shovelled their own paths across the ice. Marie's brothers cleared a long, winding lane from their house to the market so the family could skate there to buy bread. 3 Today, the Rideau Canal Skateway is cleared by machines and is one of the longest skating rinks in the world.
